Deployment

Where do the Brain and Devbox run?

Cognition documents Enterprise Cloud and Customer Dedicated Devbox placements while saying the Brain remains in Cognition Cloud.

Runtime · Deployment

Cognition documents Devin as a Brain plus Devbox architecture: the Brain remains in Cognition Cloud, while Enterprise Cloud runs each session's Devbox on an isolated Cognition-hosted machine and Customer Dedicated runs Devboxes in a customer-isolated single-tenant VPC connected through AWS PrivateLink or IPSec.

Principal and attribution

Whose identity creates and owns a session?

Cognition distinguishes service-user and human credentials and requires separate permissions when a service user creates a session on behalf of a human.

Authority · Identity

Cognition's authentication reference distinguishes service-user API keys from closed-beta human Personal Access Tokens; says service-user-created sessions are attributed to the service user by default; and requires ImpersonateOrgSessions when create_as_user_id attributes a session to a specific human user.

Approval chain

Which human approvals can occur before planning, actions and desktop QA?

Current planning can auto-proceed after a feedback window or wait for explicit approval; safe mode can await action approval; publisher configuration guidance says bypass approval removes manual approval for named scheduled actions; Devin 2.2 separately requested approval before desktop QA.

Authority · Approval

Cognition's current Interactive Planning documentation says Devin waits thirty seconds for feedback by default before automatically proceeding, permits the timing behavior to be adjusted, and offers a Wait for my approval control that prevents autonomous execution until plan feedback is supplied.

Repository authority

What GitHub access does Cognition say the integration requests?

The GitHub App can be limited to selected repositories or granted all organization repositories and requests multiple read and read/write permissions, including contents, issues, pull requests and workflows.

Authority · Repository

Cognition's current GitHub integration documentation says an administrator can grant Devin all organization repositories or selected repositories and that the GitHub App requests read/write access for checks, commit statuses, contents, discussions, issues, pull requests, projects and workflows so Devin can push branches, open pull requests and participate in pull-request discussions.

Record limitations

  • All product claims are attributed to Cognition public sources; no behavior was observed.
  • No Devin account, service, API, session, model, Devbox, integration, tenant or outpost was installed, invoked or inspected.
  • Devin 2.2 and API v3 are dated service and API milestones, not immutable current service builds.
  • Enterprise Cloud and Customer Dedicated share a Cognition Cloud Brain but have different Devbox, tenant and network boundaries.
  • The API schema establishes selectable fields and status meanings, not their effective value in any session.
  • A service-user permission does not establish a particular session's target user, repository authority or audit attribution.
  • Plan approval, safe-mode action approval, approval bypass and desktop-QA approval are different gates and are not collapsed.
  • The desktop-QA approval claim is scoped to the Devin 2.2 release note and is not silently rolled forward.
  • GitHub App permissions are publisher-declared authorization requirements, not proof that any repository action occurred.
  • Secure Mode's stated effect does not identify a complete egress policy or prove enforcement.
  • The compound-system description does not identify an exact model or model-serving revision.
  • No independent evaluation passed independence, exact applicability, disclosure and public-artifact gates.
  • No performance, correctness, quality, safety, privacy, containment or approval-enforcement conclusion is supported.
